write.prompt: More and more young people now listen to audiobooks or read on screens instead of reading printed books. What are the reasons for this change, and do you think it is a good or bad development?
mustUse: thesis trả lời cả hai câu hỏi
nêu rõ nguyên nhân chính và phụ
đánh giá có lý do (có thể kèm điều kiện)
write.modelAfterSubmit:
Many young people today listen to audiobooks on the bus or read stories on their phones rather than holding a printed book. This change is mainly caused by the convenience of smartphones, and in my view it is largely a positive development, as long as young people still practise deep reading.

The main reason is that a phone is always within reach. A single device can store hundreds of books, and many e-books are cheaper than printed ones, so students can start reading almost anywhere. A secondary reason is lack of time. With long school days and extra classes, many teenagers find that their only free moments come on the way to school or while doing chores, and audiobooks fit these moments perfectly.

On the positive side, these formats help young people keep reading for pleasure despite their busy lives. Readers can adjust the font size, and listeners can enjoy a story while jogging or travelling. However, there is a risk. When books are read on a phone, games and short videos are only one tap away, which may weaken readers' ability to concentrate on a long text.

In conclusion, young people are turning to audiobooks and screens mainly because they are convenient. This trend is positive overall, provided that readers switch off notifications and still make time for longer, focused reading.
